title: Partner Co-sell Pipeline Review - Lynx Integrations
summary: Quarterly co-sell pipeline review to align on top joint opportunities, discuss handoff process, pricing expectations, and next steps for running a joint demo and pilot. Redwood AE + SE present; customer reps outlined 3 prioritized deals and asked for technical benchmarks and co-sell collateral.
next_steps: Jamie to share updated co-sell deck and pricing spreadsheet (by 2026-10-08)
Priya to schedule a joint technical deep-dive and benchmark run for Deal A (by 2026-10-12)
Carlos to confirm stakeholder list and procurement timeline for Deal B (by 2026-10-09)
Evan to add Lynx to co-sell tracking sheet and invite to next partner sync (by 2026-10-07)
action_items: Jamie Carter - send updated co-sell deck and pricing spreadsheet - 2026-10-08
Priya Nair - coordinate benchmark environment and test dataset for Deal A - 2026-10-12
Carlos Mendez - share procurement timeline and legal contact for Deal B - 2026-10-09
Evan Li - add Lynx deals to co-sell tracker and invite to next sync - 2026-10-07
transcript:
[00:00:00] Jamie Carter: All right everyone, thanks for joining, I think were just waiting on Maya for a sec. Uh welcome Lynx team, appreciate you carving out time for the co-sell pipeline review.
[00:00:18] Carlos Mendez: Hey Jamie, thanks, yeah sorry we are a touch delayed, had a quick exec sync. Happy to be here.
[00:00:25] Jamie Carter: No worries, we'll run through the top three deals we identified, quick status and any blockers, then Priya will cover technical asks.
[00:00:33] Maya Patel: Hi all, Maya here, good to meet you, excited to sync.
[00:00:39] Priya Nair: Hi team. Quick note on agenda - Deal A is healthcare customer, high latency sensitivity; Deal B is fintech pilot with residency requirements; Deal C is internal Lynx integration evaluation.
[00:00:57] Tom Lee: Yeah for Deal A we did initial discovery last week, CTO cares a lot about latency under 200ms and SOC2 compliance.
[00:01:08] Aisha Khan: And for Deal B it's really about data residency and key management, they want BYOK and HSM support, plus audit logs.
[00:01:18] Jamie Carter: That's helpful. From Redwood side were proposing a hosted API for the initial POC for speed, with option to switch to Dedicated or Private for production if residency or compliance demands it.
[00:01:34] Carlos Mendez: Can you remind us again of the tradeoffs? Cost versus latency etc. I know our sales team wants clear talking points.
[00:01:43] Priya Nair: Sure - hosted is fastest to stand up and lowest operational overhead. Dedicated gives you predictable throughput and lower per-token unit cost at scale. Private (VPC/on-prem) is the choice if you need strict data residency or full control of the network and KMS. There is also quantization guidance that can reduce costs without much quality drop in many cases.
[00:02:05] Tom Lee: On the latency ask - is 200ms realistic? What's the typical p95 you see?
[00:02:12] Priya Nair: For shorter context lengths and the models we're recommending, p95 can be in the 120-220ms ballpark for hosted depending on region and request size; Dedicated can tighten that with right GPU config and batching policy. There is variance though, and we always recommend a short benchmarking run.
[00:02:29] Maya Patel: Do you have perf benchmarks we can share with the customer?
[00:02:34] Jamie Carter: Yes, I'll share our co-sell folder - there's a perf spreadsheet and recommended configs.
[00:02:39] Carlos Mendez: Great. Also, margins - what does the co-sell split look like? Our RevOps wants a clear margin breakdown so they know the partner cut.
[00:02:48] Evan Li: For initial pilots we typically do a discount to support the partner motion, and for closed ARR deals we have partner-specific compensation that we can outline. Jamie will follow up with the exact pricing table.
[00:02:58] Aisha Khan: On security, customer asked about SOC2, ISO, SSO/SAML and audit logs.
[00:03:05] Priya Nair: We have SOC2 and ISO documents; SAML/SSO and RBAC are supported in our Console; audit logs are available in Dedicated/Private options. We can share the security pack.
[00:03:16] Tom Lee: For Deal B they need BYOK - is HSM integration GA?
[00:03:21] Jamie Carter: Yes BYOK via KMS is supported for Private and Dedicated, HSM options via partner integrations are available, we'll send the details.
[00:03:30] Carlos Mendez: Okay, timing - Deal A wants an internal demo next week and a pilot kickoff in two weeks if the demo lands.
[00:03:39] Priya Nair: We can do a joint demo, and we should run a small benchmark ahead of pilot to set expectations. Suggest Priya and Tom schedule that.
[00:03:49] Tom Lee: Sounds good.
[00:03:52] Maya Patel: Quick question - how do you handle failure modes? For the healthcare customer if latency spikes or model falls back, we need graceful degradation.
[00:04:02] Priya Nair: We have smart routing and automated fallback policies to keep apps online; can route to smaller, cheaper variants or different region. We'll document IMHO recomendations.
[00:04:14] Carlos Mendez: Who's the escalation path if the customer hits issues during pilot?
[00:04:18] Jamie Carter: AE is primary contact, we loop in SE and Partner Ops; for Dedicated/Private there are SLA contacts in the contract. Evan will own the co-sell tracking and escalation matrix.
[00:04:29] [00:05:00] Jamie Carter: (brief aside) Also wanted to flag one of the larger deals in our mutual pipeline, the Telco opportunity - could be a multi-region Dedicated sale if it progresses.
[00:05:10] Aisha Khan: Any regulatory concerns for that telco?
[00:05:14] Priya Nair: Telco may have residency and audit needs similar to fintech, we'd likely recommend Dedicated or Private with on-prem options.
[00:05:24] Carlos Mendez: Back to Deal A specifics - they use a 2k token context heavily, how does that change perf and cost?
[00:05:33] Priya Nair: Longer contexts increase cost and latency. For 2k tokens batching and KV cache behavior matters; we can provide model/quantization suggestions to mitigate.
[00:05:43] Tom Lee: For the POC dataset, theyre planning to drop about 50k requests over two weeks.
[00:05:49] Priya Nair: That's a good size for a POC; we'll recommend burst config and a dedicated slot during the benchmark run so results are stable.
[00:06:00] Jamie Carter: Next item - enablement. Lynx sellers need a one-pager with key talking points: "when to position Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private" and cost estimates.
[00:06:11] Maya Patel: Yes please, reps need simple decision flow.
[00:06:15] Jamie Carter: We'll create that and include example TCO for the three profile sizes.
[00:06:22] [00:06:45] Carlos Mendez: A potential blocker is procurement cadence - Deal B's procurement window is tight, they may require 60-day legal review.
[00:06:54] Jamie Carter: We can provide standard contract addendum and our legal contact to speed that up; Evan will coordinate.
[00:07:04] Aisha Khan: A technical ask - can Redwood support function calling / tool calls for our customer's agent orchestration? They require structured output and tool invocation.
[00:07:15] Priya Nair: Yes, function/tool calling is supported in the hosted API and console workflow; we'll share examples and a reference repo.
[00:07:25] Tom Lee: For benchmarking what metrics should we capture? Latency p50/p95, token cost, error rate, throughput?
[00:07:33] Priya Nair: Exactly - p50/p95, token cost, throughput, and quality metrics on a holdout prompt set. We'll include a small eval harness.
[00:07:44] Maya Patel: Can you also include guidance on model fallbacks and expected semantic drift when switching quantized variants?
[00:07:52] Priya Nair: Yes, we'll include recommended model variants and quality expectations; note that heavy quantization may affect fine-grained reasoning so well recommend prompt tuning and evals.
[00:08:05] [00:08:40] Jamie Carter: Quick check - do you want Redwood running the benchmark or do you want to run it yourselves?
[00:08:46] Carlos Mendez: Ideally Redwood runs the initial benchmark with your baseline environment so we have apples-to-apples numbers. Then we can iterate.
[00:08:55] Jamie Carter: Good, we'll set that up. Priya will own the run.
[00:09:00] Aisha Khan: One ask - can you provide an SLA tiers doc and estimated uplift for guaranteed latency SLO?
[00:09:08] Evan Li: Yes, we can share SLA tiers and uplift pricing for tighter latency SLOs.
[00:09:14] Tom Lee: Are there any limitations with our customer's existing cloud accounts? They prefer GCP region us-west1.
[00:09:21] Priya Nair: We support multiple regions; well validate region availability for the model family they need and call that out in the bench.
[00:09:29] [00:09:55] Maya Patel: From Lynx ops perspective, we need a clear partner playbook - who owns pre-sales, who owns procurement, and the handoff matrix.
[00:10:04] Jamie Carter: We'll draft a playbook and include a handoff checklist. Evan will draft initial doc.
[00:10:10] Carlos Mendez: Any competitive risks? Customer mentioned they talked to Cohere and OpenAI.
[00:10:18] Priya Nair: Typical. We'll highlight our production-first features: dedicated runtime, caching, rollout controls, and cost controls that are attractive for these workloads.
[00:10:28] Aisha Khan: Will there be a reseller agreement or do we execute direct with the customer?
[00:10:34] Jamie Carter: We usually do direct contracting with partner-friendly terms; we can align on specifics per deal.
[00:10:40] [00:11:10] Tom Lee: Quick nitty-gritty - what logging level do you expose for request traces? We need token-level latency and cost.
[00:11:18] Priya Nair: Console exposes token-level cost and latency, per-route dashboards, and tracing hooks. For deeper logs we can do X-out or share more detailed traces under NDA.
[00:11:30] Jamie Carter: Ok wrapping up, recap of owners and dates: I'll send deck and pricing by 10/08, Priya will schedule benchmark and run by 10/12, Evan will update co-sell tracker by 10/07, Carlos to confirm procurement timeline by 10/09.
[00:11:51] Carlos Mendez: That works. Thanks everybody.
[00:11:54] Maya Patel: Thanks all, excited to get momentum on these.
[00:12:00] Jamie Carter: Great, well follow up in email with links - thanks.
[00:12:05] [end of recorded transcript - rest of call used to confirm calendar invites and quick intros, informal chat omitted]
